name: Sunwing (ex-Sunwing jets flown by WestJet)
description: Sunwing Airlines' scheme, still worn by its 737-800s and 737 MAX 8s now flying for WestJet after Sunwing was folded in: a white fuselage with 'sunwing' in orange lower case over the forward windows and a small Canadian flag under the cockpit; the orange fin sweeps forward along the crown and down round the rear fuselage behind the aft door, the tail cone orange; 'sunwing' in white up the fin; orange engines with Sunwing's white sun.

areas.name: orange sweeping forward from the fin along the crown and down round the rear fuselage behind the aft door; the tail cone orange

logos.description: Sunwing's sun, white on the orange cowling: a small open ring with eight short rays round it.
A small Canadian flag under the cockpit windows.

titles.style: Sunwing's wordmark: bold rounded lower case in orange over the forward windows, from behind the forward door.
The wordmark in white up the fin, reading upward toward the tip's trailing corner.

notes: Sunwing Airlines (SWG) was folded into WestJet in 2025; its 737s fly on as WestJet (WJA callsigns) in Sunwing's paint until they're repainted, so the scheme sits under WJA. Drawn on C-FMXG (MAX 8, left side, 2025-02-27), the most side-on open photo, fitted to the measured shape; the orange's edge is a smooth sweep (the photos show it curved, as Sunwing paints it, not a stripe). C-FJVE (2025-10) and C-FMXG and C-GFEH (2026-03) show it current. The belly under the sweep is assumed orange from the edge back. The fin's small sun over the 'w' (on C-FJVE) isn't drawn. Winglets: the 737-800's blended winglets are orange with 'sunwing' in white (C-FJVE); on the MAX the split winglet's lower blade is navy (C-FMXG), drawn orange.
